body:
Futni Mentem is one of the most infuriating films I've ever had the misfortune to sit through. Every single second grated on my nerves - from the paper-thin plot to the cringe-inducing dialogue and the painfully unfunny attempts at humor. Even the commercials around it somehow managed to be irritating.

The characters are hollow, the writing feels like it was cobbled together in five minutes, and the tone is so forced it's almost insulting. Watching it wasn't entertainment; it was endurance training. The real accomplishment here isn't making the film - it's that I somehow made it to the end alive...

Average movie, average acting, full of clichés, a little bit boring, not very funny, the scenes are nice, the shooting is OK, we have some beautiful pictures here. I hated the Füstli commercials, so cheap, that is a terrible trash junk food brand in Hungary. Dorottya Udvaros is a fine actress in Hungary, she is the best in this movie.

It was mostly incredibly embarrassing to watch, as both the story and the dialogues were just so badly written. The phone calls were so awfully timed that it was ridiculous.

100% predictable storylines from beginning to end, no depth of characters, no unexpected twists, full of clichés, this movie experience is not where Hungarian cinema should be in 2025.

I feel like the actors were struggling to naturally act out the situations their characters were put into, and I could not emphasize or relate to any of these characters.

The reason that I do not give 1 stars is because it was half decently filmed, lit and cut. I am astonished that currently its rating is over 7.

This film isn't going to change the world, but it carries some beautiful messages about various themes, such as grief, giving up, and commitment. The story has a nice arc, though it's quite grounded and nothing particularly awe-inspiring.

Perhaps for the first time in a Hungarian film, the child actor outperforms some of the adults.

Aside from a few very minor surprises, the whole story is fairly predictable after the first 15 minutes, but still it has nice moments.

In my opinion, this film was made for a primarily female audience in mind. As a man, I found it harder to relate to the characters and their struggles, but it is okay.

In recent years, a good quality Hungarian film is as rare as the White Raven. Most are either very weak or just mediocre...

This film is entertaining, funny, interesting, the characters are good and the story is good. It was enjoyable to watch this film. Congratulations to the makers!!!! Even at the end, my faith returns that Hungarian films can be good.

The story is entertaining, hilarious, how the vicissitudes of marathon training and finding a partner are connected. I can only recommend watching the film.

Congratulations to the makers, they deserve it!!!! We need more good stories and movies like this.
